# Requirements Quality Checklist: Topic Complexity Filtering

**Purpose**: Reviewer-oriented quality checks for requirement completeness, clarity, and measurability of topic complexity filtering.
**Created**: 2026-08-27
**Feature**: [specs/004-topic-complexity-filter/spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements explicitly defined for default filter state, control placement, and available complexity options? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001..FR-003]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements explicitly defined for both all-topics behavior and single-complexity behavior? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004..FR-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements explicitly defined for combined search-and-complexity behavior rather than independent filtering only? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK004 Are topic metadata requirements complete enough to identify mandatory complexity classification for every topic record? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK005 Are no-results requirements complete for both complexity-only and search-plus-complexity empty states? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is the phrase "displayed beside the search bar" specific enough to avoid multiple valid layout interpretations? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §Acceptance Scenario 1]
- [ ] CHK007 Is "default to All" unambiguous about when reset happens (initial load only versus every route revisit)? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK008 Are allowed complexity values and casing conventions defined to prevent mismatched labels (for example easy/Easy)? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the handling of topics with missing complexity consistently defined between edge cases and data assumptions? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the no-results feedback requirement specific enough to be objectively reviewed for adequacy? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Do requirement statements and acceptance scenarios consistently describe AND semantics for search plus complexity filtering? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, Spec §Acceptance Scenario 4]
- [ ] CHK012 Do assumptions and edge-case rules stay consistent about whether `Unknown` complexity is allowed and how it is treated? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK013 Do success criteria and functional requirements use consistent terms for filter state and visible-topic expectations? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004..FR-006, Spec §SC-001..SC-002]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK014 Can each acceptance scenario be evaluated objectively without adding unstated interpretation rules? [Measurability, Spec §Acceptance Scenarios]
- [ ] CHK015 Are success metrics for correctness and discoverability measurable and bounded with clear pass/fail thresholds? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001..SC-004]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the audience/sample definition for user acceptance measurement sufficiently specified to avoid inconsistent evaluation methods? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §SC-003]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK017 Are primary, alternate, and combined-filter journeys fully represented in requirements and scenarios? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 4, Spec §Acceptance Scenarios]
- [ ] CHK018 Are route-level variations across all in-scope topic groups explicitly covered by requirements or assumptions? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for behavior when users change complexity while a search query is already active? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-006]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK020 Are boundary conditions documented for zero matches and missing complexity metadata? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK021 Are malformed or unexpected complexity values addressed, or explicitly excluded from scope? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-007]

## Non-Functional Requirements Quality

- [ ] CHK022 Are accessibility requirements for filter discoverability, labeling, and keyboard use explicitly documented in the feature spec? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §User Scenarios]
- [ ] CHK023 Are responsiveness/performance expectations for filter interactions quantified enough for consistent acceptance review? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §SC-003]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK024 Are dependencies on enriching existing topic datasets with complexity values explicitly traceable and bounded? [Dependency, Assumption, Spec §FR-007, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK025 Are out-of-scope boundaries (for example persistence across sessions and user-role differences) clearly documented to prevent scope drift? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK026 Is there any unresolved ambiguity between "display all topics" and exclusion of `Unknown` in non-All views that should be normalized into explicit rules? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004..FR-005, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK027 Are any conflicting interpretations left between requirement text and measurable outcomes for default state behavior? [Conflict, Spec §FR-003, Spec §SC-004]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline during review.
